questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is startled by a nearby explosion, and his circulating epinephrine surges. In addition to its direct effects on liver, skeletal muscle, and adipose tissue, which of the following effects does epinephrine exert on the pancreatic islets?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stimulates insulin release from β-cells and inhibits glucagon release from α-cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stimulates both insulin release from β-cells and glucagon release from α-cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibits both insulin release from β-cells and glucagon release from α-cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Has no effect on either β-cell insulin release or α-cell glucagon release

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulates glucagon release from α-cells and inhibits insulin release from β-cells

explanation.summary: Epinephrine stimulates α-cell glucagon release and inhibits β-cell insulin release, reinforcing fuel mobilization.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the epinephrine signaling figure, the pancreas shows a stimulatory signal on glucagon from the α-cell and a stop signal on insulin from the β-cell. This complements epinephrine's direct actions of promoting glycogen breakdown in liver and muscle and hormone-sensitive lipase activity in adipocytes to keep fuel available during fight-or-flight.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is backwards; insulin promotes storage, which would oppose the fuel mobilization epinephrine seeks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epinephrine does not stimulate insulin release; it inhibits the β-cell while stimulating the α-cell.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucagon release is stimulated, not inhibited, by epinephrine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Epinephrine does act on the islets, promoting glucagon and suppressing insulin.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: During a sprint, epinephrine stimulates glycogenolysis in skeletal muscle. Because skeletal muscle cannot export free glucose, which of the following best describes how muscle glycogen ultimately contributes to hepatic glucose production in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Muscle releases pyruvate and lactate, which the liver uses to synthesize glucose

choices.label: B
choices.text: Muscle releases glucose 6-phosphate, which the liver dephosphorylates to glucose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Muscle releases glycerol, which the liver phosphorylates for gluconeogenesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Muscle releases glycogen fragments that hepatic glycogen phosphorylase degrades

choices.label: E
choices.text: Muscle releases fatty acids that the liver converts to glucose via β-oxidation

explanation.summary: Under epinephrine, muscle glycogen is catabolized to pyruvate and lactate, which travel to the liver to be made into glucose.
explanation.whyCorrect: The epinephrine signaling figure shows muscle glycogen breakdown yielding pyruvate and lactate that flow to the liver, where they feed glucose production alongside glycerol from adipose tissue. Muscle lacks glucose 6-phosphatase, so it cannot release free glucose directly.

whyWrongByChoice.B: GLUTs cannot transport phosphorylated glucose, so glucose 6-phosphate is not exported from muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycerol is released from adipocyte triglycerides by hormone-sensitive lipase, not from muscle glycogen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycogen is degraded within the myocyte; intact glycogen fragments are not released into the circulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fatty acids are supplied by adipocytes and are oxidized for ATP in the liver; β-oxidation does not convert them to glucose.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A 25-year-old marathon runner follows a high-carbohydrate diet for several days before a race. Once her hepatic and skeletal muscle glycogen stores reach their maximal capacity, which of the following is the predominant fate of additional dietary glucose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Storage as glycogen within adipocytes for later mobilization

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion to fatty acids via acetyl-CoA carboxylase for storage in adipocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conversion to amino acids for expansion of the free amino acid pool

choices.label: D
choices.text: Storage as glycogen within the brain to buffer hypoglycemia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Conversion to ketone bodies for oxidation by cardiac muscle

explanation.summary: Once glycogen stores are full, excess glucose is diverted into fatty acid synthesis via acetyl-CoA carboxylase for long-term storage in adipocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Glycogen stores are not limitless. While glucose-rich diets maximize glycogen in liver and skeletal muscle, these stores reach a maximum capacity, after which excess glucose is diverted into fatty acid production via acetyl-CoA carboxylase for long-term storage in adipocytes, whose triglyceride capacity is limitless.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adipocytes store triglycerides, not glycogen; glycogen depots are the liver and skeletal muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The free amino acid pool is fairly static and is not an expandable depot for excess carbons.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brain does not store glycogen, which is why it depends on circulating glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ketone bodies are a fasting fuel, not a storage form for excess dietary glucose.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: Which of the following energy depots is described as having limitless capacity for expansion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycogen within hepatocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glycogen within skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Triglycerides within adipocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The free amino acid pool

choices.label: E
choices.text: Circulating plasma glucose

explanation.summary: Adipocytes are the only cells with limitless capacity for expansion, so triglyceride storage is limitless.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adipocytes are the only cells in the body that have limitless capacity of expansion. In contrast to glycogen, triglyceride formation and storage within adipocytes is limitless, and this stored energy is released by glucagon or epinephrine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hepatic glycogen reaches a maximum capacity, after which excess glucose is diverted to fatty acids.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Muscle glycogen likewise has a finite maximum capacity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The free amino acid pool is fairly static; proteins do not primarily serve as storage sites for amino acids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasma glucose is held within a narrow window rather than serving as an expandable depot.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman has been fasting for 18 hours. Hormone-sensitive lipase in her adipocytes hydrolyzes stored triglycerides. Which of the following correctly pairs each product with its predominant metabolic fate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycerol: β-oxidation in skeletal muscle; fatty acids: hepatic gluconeogenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glycerol: direct oxidation by the brain; fatty acids: glycolysis in red blood cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycerol: re-esterification within adipocytes; fatty acids: hepatic glycogen synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glycerol: hepatic gluconeogenesis; fatty acids: β-oxidation in muscle and liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glycerol: conversion to ketone bodies in liver; fatty acids: storage as muscle glycogen

explanation.summary: Triglyceride hydrolysis yields glycerol for hepatic gluconeogenesis and three fatty acids for β-oxidation in tissues such as muscle and liver.
explanation.whyCorrect: Upon degradation, triglycerides yield glycerol and three fatty acids. The fatty acids are consumed by a variety of tissues such as muscle and liver through β-oxidation, while the glycerol backbone is predominantly used by the liver as a substrate for gluconeogenesis, which is possible because the liver expresses glycerol kinase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This reverses the fates: glycerol is a gluconeogenic substrate and fatty acids undergo β-oxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fatty acids are not a brain or red blood cell fuel; the brain uses glucose (or ketones in prolonged fasting) and RBCs use glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adipocytes lack glycerol kinase, so released glycerol cannot be re-esterified locally and instead exits to the liver.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glycerol feeds gluconeogenesis rather than ketogenesis, and fatty acids are not converted to muscle glycogen.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: In hepatocytes, glycerol kinase catalyzes a reversible reaction between glycerol and glycerol 3-phosphate. Which of the following sets of conditions most strongly favors formation of glycerol 3-phosphate from glycerol?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Insulin present, high DHAP from glycolysis, low glycerol from lipolysis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Insulin present, low ATP from β-oxidation, high DHAP from glycolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucagon present, low ATP from β-oxidation, low glycerol from lipolysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin present, high ATP from glycolysis, high DHAP from glycolysis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glucagon present, high ATP from β-oxidation, high glycerol from lipolysis

explanation.summary: Glucagon, high ATP from fatty acid β-oxidation, and abundant glycerol from adipocyte lipolysis drive glycerol kinase toward glycerol 3-phosphate for gluconeogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Glycerol 3-phosphate formation is favored when glucagon is present, ATP is high due to β-oxidation of fatty acids, and glycerol is high due to release from adipocyte triglycerides by hormone-sensitive lipase. Under these fasting conditions the glycerol 3-phosphate is converted by glycerol 3-phosphate dehydrogenase to DHAP for gluconeogenesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Insulin and high DHAP favor the reverse direction, forming glycerol from glycolytic intermediates for VLDL triglyceride synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Insulin with high DHAP and low ATP does not favor phosphorylating glycerol; it favors glycerol formation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucagon alone is insufficient when ATP and glycerol substrate are both low; the fasting drive requires high ATP and high glycerol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Insulin with abundant glycolytic DHAP favors glycerol formation for triglyceride and VLDL synthesis, not glycerol 3-phosphate formation from glycerol.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: In the fed state, adipocytes synthesize triglycerides, a process that requires glycerol 3-phosphate. Given that adipocytes lack glycerol kinase, which of the following is the source of the glycerol 3-phosphate used for adipocyte triglyceride synthesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduction of DHAP formed by glycolysis of glucose entering via GLUT4

choices.label: B
choices.text: Phosphorylation of glycerol recaptured after hormone-sensitive lipase acts on triglycerides

choices.label: C
choices.text: Phosphorylation of free glycerol delivered to the adipocyte by circulating VLDL

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduction of DHAP generated during β-oxidation of incoming fatty acids

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uptake of glycerol 3-phosphate exported by hepatocytes into the circulation

explanation.summary: Adipocytes make glycerol 3-phosphate only from glycolytic DHAP when glucose is abundant and insulin drives GLUT4-mediated uptake.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adipocytes only make glycerol 3-phosphate when glucose is abundant. Insulin signaling promotes glucose uptake through GLUT4 and glycolytic production of DHAP, which is then reduced to form glycerol 3-phosphate for triglyceride synthesis. Fatty acids for the triglycerides arrive from the diet via chylomicrons or from the liver via VLDL.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Adipocytes lack glycerol kinase, so glycerol released by hormone-sensitive lipase cannot be phosphorylated and instead exits the cell.
whyWrongByChoice.C: VLDL supplies fatty acids through lipoprotein lipase, and any free glycerol could not be phosphorylated by adipocytes anyway.
whyWrongByChoice.D: β-oxidation does not generate DHAP; DHAP is a glycolytic intermediate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glycerol 3-phosphate is not exported by the liver into the blood; adipocytes generate it internally from glucose.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: Compared with the glycogen and triglyceride depots, which of the following best characterizes the free amino acid pool in a healthy human?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It expands markedly after a protein-rich meal and contracts during fasting

choices.label: B
choices.text: It remains fairly static, since proteins are not primarily amino acid storage sites

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the body's largest energy reserve and is mobilized before glycogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is stored within adipocytes alongside triglycerides for later release

choices.label: E
choices.text: It cannot be catabolized to supply substrates for OXPHOS or gluconeogenesis

explanation.summary: Unlike fat and glycogen depots, the free amino acid pool is fairly static because proteins are not primarily storage sites for amino acids.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fats and glycogen are depots that can expand and retract, but the free amino acid pool is fairly static within a human. While proteins can be catabolized to generate amino acids, proteins do not function primarily as storage sites for amino acids; hormonal influence can nonetheless drive catabolism to produce substrates for OXPHOS or gluconeogenesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Expansion and contraction describe the glycogen and fat depots, not the relatively static amino acid pool.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Triglyceride in adipocytes is the limitless energy reserve; the amino acid pool is not a primary energy depot.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adipocytes store triglycerides, not amino acids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hormonal influence can drive amino acid catabolism to supply substrates for OXPHOS or gluconeogenesis.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: After a carbohydrate-rich meal, insulin binds its receptor on hepatocytes and promotes glycogen synthesis. Which of the following signaling sequences mediates this effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenylate cyclase → cAMP → protein kinase A → phosphorylation of glycogen synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ca2+ release → calmodulin → phosphorylase kinase → activation of glycogen synthase

choices.label: C
choices.text: PI3-kinase → PKB/Akt → protein phosphatase → dephosphorylation of glycogen synthase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intracellular receptor binding → altered gene expression → induction of glycogen synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adenylate kinase → AMP → allosteric activation of glycogen synthase

explanation.summary: Insulin acts through PI3-kinase and PKB/Akt to activate protein phosphatases that dephosphorylate and activate glycogen synthase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Activation of the insulin receptor promotes the PI3-kinase cascade, which activates PKB/Akt and culminates in activation of protein phosphatases. In the liver, insulin removes phosphate from glycogen synthase to activate it and promote glycogen synthesis, while also dephosphorylating and inactivating phosphorylase kinase and glycogen phosphorylase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The adenylate cyclase/cAMP/PKA route is glucagon's pathway, and PKA phosphorylation inactivates glycogen synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ca2+-calmodulin activates phosphorylase kinase in contracting muscle to promote glycogen breakdown, not synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intracellular receptor binding and gene expression describe cortisol, a steroid, not insulin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: AMP allosterically activates glycogen phosphorylase during muscle contraction; it is not an insulin signal.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A healthy adult continues to eat a high-carbohydrate diet after hepatic glycogen stores are full. Sustained insulin signaling increases hepatic glycolysis through production of fructose 2,6-bisphosphate by PFK-2. Under these conditions, the acetyl-CoA generated in the liver is predominantly used for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oxidation in the TCA cycle to maximize hepatic ATP production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion to ketone bodies for export to the brain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gluconeogenesis to replenish circulating glucose

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fatty acid synthesis via dephosphorylated acetyl-CoA carboxylase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glycogen synthesis via activated glycogen synthase

explanation.summary: With glycogen full, sustained insulin drives hepatic glycolysis whose acetyl-CoA feeds fatty acid synthesis through dephosphorylated, active acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Insulin initially replenishes hepatic glycogen; sustained insulin signaling results in lipogenesis. Hepatic glycolysis is stimulated via fructose 2,6-bisphosphate to promote acetyl-CoA formation, but this acetyl-CoA does not serve as a TCA substrate; it provides substrate for fatty acid synthesis so excess carbons are stored, largely achieved by dephosphorylation of acetyl-CoA carboxylase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The brick specifically notes this acetyl-CoA does not serve as a TCA substrate under sustained insulin signaling.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ketone body production is a fasting response, not a fed-state fate of glycolytic acetyl-CoA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gluconeogenesis is inhibited by insulin, and acetyl-CoA is not being routed to glucose in the fed state.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glycogen synthase uses glucose-derived units, not acetyl-CoA, and glycogen stores are already at capacity in this scenario.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A liver biopsy from a subject who has fasted overnight is analyzed for enzyme phosphorylation state. Which of the following hepatic enzymes would be expected to be both phosphorylated and active under these conditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycogen synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pyruvate kinase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase

choices.label: D
choices.text: PFK-2 (kinase activity)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glycogen phosphorylase

explanation.summary: Glucagon-driven PKA phosphorylates catabolic enzymes such as glycogen phosphorylase to activate them and synthetic enzymes to inhibit them.
explanation.whyCorrect: Glucagon-dependent stimulation of PKA undoes the action of insulin by adding phosphate groups onto catabolic enzymes for activation and synthetic enzymes for inhibition. PKA phosphorylates phosphorylase kinase, which then phosphorylates glycogen phosphorylase to activate it and promote glycogen degradation during fasting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glycogen synthase is phosphorylated during fasting, but phosphorylation inactivates this synthetic enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pyruvate kinase is phosphorylated by PKA to slow hepatic glycolysis, so it is phosphorylated but inhibited.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase is activated by dephosphorylation under insulin; during fasting it is phosphorylated and inactive.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glucagon influences PFK-2 to favor its phosphatase activity, so its kinase activity is dampened, not active.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: Thirty minutes after a large meal, lipolysis in a healthy person's adipocytes ceases. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which insulin halts triglyceride hydrolysis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A protein phosphatase downstream of PKB/Akt dephosphorylates and inactivates hormone-sensitive lipase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Protein kinase A activated by cAMP phosphorylates and inactivates hormone-sensitive lipase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycerol accumulating within the adipocyte allosterically inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lipoprotein lipase competes with hormone-sensitive lipase for the same triglyceride substrate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ca2+-calmodulin binds hormone-sensitive lipase and blocks its access to triglyceride droplets

explanation.summary: Insulin prevents triglyceride hydrolysis by dephosphorylating and inactivating hormone-sensitive lipase through a PI3K/PKB/Akt-activated protein phosphatase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Glucagon causes hydrolysis of triglycerides via PKA-mediated phosphorylation of hormone-sensitive lipase. In contrast, insulin, signaling through PI3K and PKB/Akt to a protein phosphatase, prevents triglyceride hydrolysis by dephosphorylating and inactivating hormone-sensitive lipase, while favoring glucose uptake and triglyceride formation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: PKA phosphorylation of hormone-sensitive lipase activates it; this is the glucagon and epinephrine mechanism for lipolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycerol exits adipocytes because they lack glycerol kinase; it is not described as an allosteric inhibitor of the lipase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lipoprotein lipase acts on circulating VLDL and chylomicron triglycerides to deliver fatty acids, not on stored droplets.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ca2+-calmodulin regulates phosphorylase kinase in contracting muscle and has no described role on hormone-sensitive lipase.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman on long-term prednisone (a cortisol derivative) for an inflammatory disease develops weight gain and impaired glucose control. The metabolic effects of this drug arise through which of the following signaling mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activation of a GPCR to raise cAMP and stimulate protein kinase A

choices.label: B
choices.text: Binding of intracellular receptors to activate gene expression

choices.label: C
choices.text: Activation of PI3-kinase and PKB/Akt via a membrane receptor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of Ca2+ and activation of calmodulin-dependent kinases

choices.label: E
choices.text: Allosteric activation of cytosolic enzymes by rising AMP

explanation.summary: Cortisol is a steroid that binds intracellular receptors to activate gene expression, producing pleiotropic effects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cortisol production is associated with the stress response. As a steroid, it binds intracellular receptors to activate gene expression, and like many steroids it is pleiotropic with numerous effects across organ systems. Cortisol and its derivatives are superb anti-inflammatory agents, but their use comes with side effects such as glucose imbalance, weight gain, and jitters.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GPCR/cAMP/PKA signaling is the mechanism of glucagon and epinephrine, not of a steroid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PI3-kinase and PKB/Akt are activated downstream of the insulin receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ca2+-calmodulin signaling links nerve impulses to glycogen breakdown in skeletal muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: AMP allosterically activates glycogen phosphorylase in contracting muscle; it is not a steroid mechanism.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is hospitalized with prolonged physiologic stress. Hepatic gluconeogenesis is markedly increased and his skeletal muscle mass is declining. Which of the following hormones is most responsible for mobilizing amino acids from muscle protein to supply gluconeogenic substrates?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Insulin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucagon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cortisol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Epinephrine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Growth hormone

explanation.summary: Cortisol stimulates amino acid mobilization from muscle protein to provide gluconeogenic substrates during stress.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cortisol provides needed fuel for changing requirements during stress. Its predominant metabolic pathways include stimulating amino acid mobilization from muscle protein for gluconeogenic substrates, stimulating gluconeogenesis to produce glucose, and stimulating fatty acid release from adipose tissue to fuel hepatic gluconeogenesis and muscle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Insulin stimulates amino acid uptake and protein synthesis, the opposite of muscle protein mobilization.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucagon activates hepatic gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis, but skeletal muscle lacks glucagon receptors, so it cannot mobilize muscle protein.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Epinephrine mobilizes glucose from glycogen and fatty acids from adipose tissue during acute stress; muscle protein mobilization is attributed to cortisol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Growth hormone is not among the hormones described as driving muscle protein catabolism for gluconeogenesis.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: Which of the following tissues relies on fatty acids as its predominant fuel even in the well-fed state?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Brain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Red blood cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adipocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cardiac muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resting skeletal muscle

explanation.summary: Cardiac muscle uses fatty acids as its fuel in the well-fed state, unlike the other listed tissues, which use glucose when fed.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the organ fuel summary, cardiac muscle is the only listed tissue that uses fatty acids in the well-fed state. During fasting it uses fatty acids plus ketone bodies, and in prolonged fasting it uses more fatty acids and fewer ketone bodies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The brain uses glucose when well-fed and fasting, shifting to ketone bodies only in prolonged fasting.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Red blood cells use glucose in every metabolic state.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adipocytes use glucose when well-fed and switch to fatty acids during fasting.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Resting skeletal muscle uses glucose when well-fed and fatty acids plus ketone bodies when fasting.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has been without food for 4 days. Compared with an overnight fast, which of the following best describes the change in fuel use by his resting skeletal muscle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Shift from fatty acids to predominantly glucose from hepatic gluconeogenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Shift from fatty acids to predominantly ketone bodies to spare glucose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shift to glycogen-derived glucose released from the muscle's own stores

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shift to lactate and pyruvate imported from red blood cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Greater reliance on fatty acids with less reliance on ketone bodies

explanation.summary: In prolonged fasting, resting skeletal muscle uses more fatty acids and fewer ketone bodies than in short-term fasting.
explanation.whyCorrect: The organ fuel summary lists resting skeletal muscle as using fatty acids and ketone bodies during fasting, but more fatty acids and less ketone bodies during prolonged fasting. Over the same period the brain shifts from glucose to ketone bodies, so the ketone supply is directed away from muscle and toward the brain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Skeletal muscle does not return to glucose during starvation; glucose is reserved for tissues such as red blood cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The trend is the opposite: muscle uses fewer ketone bodies in prolonged fasting, not more.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Muscle glycogen is consumed locally during contraction; it is not the described fuel shift of resting muscle in starvation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactate and pyruvate are exported by muscle to the liver under epinephrine; they are not a listed starvation fuel for muscle.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State

questions.stem: A researcher studies isolated pancreatic beta-cells. When extracellular glucose is raised, the cells depolarize and secrete insulin. Which of the following events most directly links glucose metabolism to membrane depolarization in these cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rising ATP closes ATP-sensitive potassium (K_ATP) channels

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rising ATP opens voltage-gated calcium channels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucose binds and directly opens calcium channels

choices.label: D
choices.text: GLUT2 actively pumps potassium out of the cell

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secreted insulin binds receptors on the same beta-cell

explanation.summary: Glucose-derived ATP closes K_ATP channels, which depolarizes the beta-cell membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: Glucose entering the beta-cell is oxidatively catabolized to generate ATP. The increased ATP acts as an allosteric inhibitor of the ATP-sensitive potassium channel, blocking potassium leak. Trapped potassium reduces the charge differential across the membrane, causing depolarization that then opens voltage-gated calcium channels.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Calcium channels are voltage-gated and open in response to the depolarization that follows K_ATP closure, not directly in response to ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucose does not directly gate calcium channels; it acts through metabolism to ATP and channel closure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GLUT2 is a facilitative glucose transporter, not a potassium pump.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin binding to peripheral receptors drives glucose uptake in muscle and fat; it is not the depolarizing trigger within the beta-cell.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with type 2 diabetes is started on a sulfonylurea to lower his blood glucose. The drug acts on pancreatic beta-cells. Which of the following best describes how it augments insulin secretion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It blocks ATP-sensitive potassium channels, promoting depolarization

choices.label: B
choices.text: It opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels to hyperpolarize the cell

choices.label: C
choices.text: It activates GLUT2 transporters to increase glucose entry

choices.label: D
choices.text: It stimulates insulin exocytosis independent of calcium

choices.label: E
choices.text: It blocks voltage-gated calcium channels

explanation.summary: Sulfonylureas close the K_ATP channel pharmacologically, bypassing the need for glucose-derived ATP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonylureas inhibit the beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channel independent of glucose metabolism. Closing the channel depolarizes the membrane, opens voltage-gated calcium channels, and drives insulin exocytosis. Because the strategy amplifies endogenous secretion, the patient's beta-cells must still be able to produce insulin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Opening the channel would hyperpolarize the cell and suppress secretion, the opposite of the drug's action.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfonylureas act on the potassium channel, not on GLUT2 glucose transport.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Secretion still depends on the downstream depolarization-triggered calcium influx.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Blocking calcium channels would prevent, not promote, insulin release.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: Pancreatic beta-cells rely on GLUT2, a transporter with a relatively high Km (low affinity) but high Vmax for glucose. What is the physiological advantage of this transporter property for insulin secretion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Substantial glucose enters the beta-cell only when blood glucose is elevated

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucose is transported into the cell against its concentration gradient

choices.label: C
choices.text: Beta-cells continue to take up glucose avidly during hypoglycemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glucose uptake by the beta-cell becomes insulin-dependent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glucose entering the cell is prevented from being oxidized

explanation.summary: GLUT2's low affinity makes beta-cell glucose uptake proportional to blood glucose, so insulin is released only when glucose is high.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because GLUT2 has low affinity, glucose flows into the beta-cell in meaningful amounts only when circulating glucose concentrations are elevated. This ensures the ATP-driven secretion cascade fires when it is needed. Having insulin present during hypoglycemia would be dangerous, driving glucose even lower and depriving the CNS.

whyWrongByChoice.B: GLUT2 is a facilitative transporter that moves glucose down its gradient, not against it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The point of low affinity is precisely that uptake is minimal during hypoglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Beta-cell uptake through GLUT2 is insulin-independent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Imported glucose is oxidatively catabolized to make the ATP that triggers secretion.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of confusion relieved by eating. During an episode she is hypoglycemic with inappropriately elevated serum insulin. To distinguish endogenous insulin overproduction (such as an insulinoma) from injection of recombinant insulin, which laboratory value is most useful?

choices.label: A
choices.text: C-peptide level

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood glucose level

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum anion gap

choices.label: D
choices.text: ALT and AST

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hemoglobin A1c

explanation.summary: C-peptide is co-secreted equimolar with endogenous insulin but is absent from recombinant insulin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endogenous insulin is packaged with C-peptide in equimolar amounts, so an insulinoma raises both insulin and C-peptide. Recombinant injected insulin lacks C-peptide entirely. Therefore a high C-peptide points to endogenous overproduction, whereas a low C-peptide with high insulin indicates an exogenous source.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood glucose is low in both scenarios and cannot separate the two causes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin excess does not produce an anion-gap acidosis, so this is unhelpful here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Insulin shock does not cause hepatocellular injury, so transaminases are not discriminating.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HbA1c reflects chronic average glycemia, not the acute source of excess insulin.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: Within the pancreatic beta-cell, proinsulin is converted into the mature, active hormone before storage. Conversion of proinsulin to mature insulin requires which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Proteolytic cleavage and release of the C-peptide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Removal of the N-terminal signal peptide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Self-assembly of the protein into a hexamer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Formation of a disulfide bond between the A and C chains

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glycosylation of the B chain

explanation.summary: Mature insulin is generated when the C-peptide is cleaved out of proinsulin, leaving the disulfide-linked A and B chains.
explanation.whyCorrect: Proinsulin already has its signal peptide removed; the final maturation step is proteolytic cleavage that releases the connecting C-peptide. This leaves the A and B chains as a disulfide-linked heterodimer, the active hormone. C-peptide and insulin are then stored equimolar in granules.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Signal peptide removal occurs earlier, converting preproinsulin to proinsulin, not proinsulin to insulin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hexamer formation is a storage/aggregation phenomenon, not the maturation cleavage step.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mature insulin's disulfide bonds link the A and B chains; the C chain is removed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin maturation is driven by proteolysis, not glycosylation.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A pharmaceutical company designs a rapid-acting insulin analog by mutating the primary sequence to prevent self-association after subcutaneous injection. This modification speeds the onset of action for which reason?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The monomer is the most active form

choices.label: B
choices.text: The hexamer is the receptor-binding active form

choices.label: C
choices.text: Monomeric insulin cannot bind the insulin receptor

choices.label: D
choices.text: The analog retains extra C-peptide to speed activation

choices.label: E
choices.text: The mutation adds disulfide bonds that stabilize the active hexamer

explanation.summary: Insulin is active as a monomer; hexamers are inactive, so blocking oligomerization gives faster action.
explanation.whyCorrect: At high concentration insulin self-associates into inactive hexamers that cannot bind the receptor. Dilution normally dissociates these into active monomers. A fast-acting analog is engineered to resist oligomerization so active monomers are available sooner, while long-acting formulations deliberately favor oligomers to slow release.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The hexamer is the inactive storage form, not the receptor-binding species.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The monomer is precisely the form that binds and activates the receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Purified injectable insulins lack C-peptide entirely.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The engineering prevents oligomerization rather than stabilizing hexamers.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A sedentary patient with type 2 diabetes is advised to exercise using large muscle groups such as the quadriceps and glutes. Exercising skeletal muscle increases glucose uptake even in the absence of insulin. This insulin-independent uptake occurs because muscle contraction does which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activates AMPK, which promotes GLUT4 translocation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stimulates insulin secretion directly from skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increases GLUT2 expression on the muscle membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Directly activates the insulin receptor tyrosine kinase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibits AMPK to conserve ATP during activity

explanation.summary: Muscle contraction consumes ATP and raises AMP, activating AMPK, which drives GLUT4 to the membrane without insulin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Contraction expends ATP and raises intracellular AMP, activating AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). AMPK promotes trafficking of pre-formed GLUT4 vesicles to the plasma membrane, so glucose uptake increases independent of insulin signaling. This is why exercise engaging large muscle masses aids glucose clearance in diabetes.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Insulin is secreted by pancreatic beta-cells, not by skeletal muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Muscle uses GLUT4, not GLUT2, and the effect is on trafficking rather than GLUT2 expression.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pathway bypasses the insulin receptor entirely, which is the defining feature of insulin-independent uptake.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Exercise activates AMPK; inhibiting it would not promote glucose uptake.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: During intense exercise, AMPK is strongly activated in skeletal muscle to restore energy balance. Which of the following processes is suppressed as a direct consequence of AMPK activation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycogenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glycolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Beta-oxidation of fatty acids

choices.label: D
choices.text: GLUT4 translocation to the membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glucose uptake into muscle

explanation.summary: AMPK inhibits ATP-consuming anabolic pathways such as glycogenesis while enhancing ATP-producing catabolism.
explanation.whyCorrect: AMPK signals a low-energy state and therefore inhibits anabolic, ATP-consuming pathways including glycogenesis, lipogenesis, and protein synthesis. It simultaneously enhances catabolic, ATP-generating processes. Of the options listed, only glycogenesis is an anabolic process suppressed by AMPK.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Glycolysis is a catabolic, ATP-producing pathway that AMPK enhances.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Beta-oxidation is catabolic and is promoted by AMPK to generate ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: AMPK promotes GLUT4 translocation to bring in glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glucose uptake is increased, not suppressed, by AMPK activation.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: AMPK monitors cellular energy status by responding to AMP. Although ATP hydrolysis primarily yields ADP, intracellular AMP rises sharply and serves as the sensitive low-energy signal. Which enzyme generates this amplified AMP signal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenylate kinase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Phosphofructokinase-1

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycogen phosphorylase

choices.label: D
choices.text: ATP synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Creatine kinase

explanation.summary: Adenylate kinase interconverts two ADP into ATP plus AMP, causing AMP to rise disproportionately during energy stress.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adenylate kinase catalyzes 2 ADP into ATP + AMP. Because baseline AMP concentrations are very low, this reaction produces a large fold-change in AMP even when ATP and ADP change little. That amplified AMP signal is what AMPK and enzymes like PFK-1 and glycogen phosphorylase sense as low energy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: PFK-1 is a glycolytic enzyme that responds to AMP; it does not generate the AMP signal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycogen phosphorylase is regulated by AMP but does not produce it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ATP synthase makes ATP from ADP and phosphate and does not generate AMP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Creatine kinase buffers ATP using phosphocreatine and does not create the AMP signal.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has been well controlled on a sulfonylurea for a year. She now reports episodes of weakness and dizziness and is found to be hypoglycemic during a visit; her symptoms resolve after glucose administration. She recently began a daily walking and cycling routine. Which change best explains her new hypoglycemic episodes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exercise-driven AMPK activation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased dietary glucose intake

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased alcohol consumption

choices.label: D
choices.text: Starting a common multivitamin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Decreased dietary sodium intake

explanation.summary: Adding exercise-induced GLUT4 uptake to a drug that already raises insulin can push glucose too low.
explanation.whyCorrect: Her sulfonylurea continuously augments insulin secretion. Daily exercise activates AMPK and deposits GLUT4 on skeletal muscle, adding insulin-independent glucose clearance. The two effects together can drive blood glucose below normal, producing the hypoglycemic episodes that resolve with glucose.

whyWrongByChoice.B: More dietary glucose would tend to raise, not lower, blood glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Alcohol can cause hypoglycemia via a high NADH/NAD+ ratio, so decreasing intake would reduce, not cause, hypoglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A standard multivitamin does not sensitize tissues to insulin or cause hypoglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reducing sodium affects blood pressure and volume, not glucose homeostasis.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A severely malnourished 22-year-old with anorexia nervosa is admitted and started on nutritional support. Shortly after carbohydrate is reintroduced, she develops profound hypophosphatemia. What is the mechanism of the falling serum phosphate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Insulin-stimulated glycolysis drives phosphate into cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucose causes renal wasting of phosphate in the urine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Her diet lacks phosphate, so serum levels simply fall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Phosphate binds administered glucose in the gut lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thiamine administration triggers hyperphosphaturia

explanation.summary: Re-feeding raises insulin, restarting glycolysis and kinase signaling that pull phosphate into cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reintroducing glucose after starvation triggers insulin secretion and restarts anabolic, phosphate-dependent processes such as glycolysis and kinase-mediated signaling. Phosphate rushes intracellularly to support these reactions, dropping serum levels. Severe hypophosphatemia in re-feeding syndrome can cause seizures, coma, or death.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The fall is due to an intracellular shift, not renal wasting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Serum phosphate can appear low-normal in starvation, but the acute drop is driven by cellular uptake, not dietary lack.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phosphate does not chelate glucose in the gut to lower serum levels.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiamine is given to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy and does not cause phosphaturia.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A liberated prisoner of war with prolonged starvation is refed with intravenous dextrose. Soon afterward he becomes confused with ophthalmoplegia and ataxia. Deficiency of which nutrient, whose demand surges when glucose is metabolized, best explains this presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Thiamin (vitamin B1)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Folate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vitamin C (ascorbate)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vitamin D

explanation.summary: Refeeding glucose without adequate thiamin precipitates Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome because thiamin is a cofactor for PDH.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thiamin is a required cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) and other enzymes of glucose oxidation. When glucose is reintroduced in a thiamin-deficient patient, the surge in demand outstrips supply, precipitating Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome with confusion, ophthalmoplegia, and ataxia. This is a key re-feeding consideration.

whyWrongByChoice.B: B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and subacute combined degeneration, not glucose-triggered encephalopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Folate deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and is not precipitated by glucose refeeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, unrelated to this acute neurologic picture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin D deficiency affects calcium and bone metabolism, not thiamin-dependent glucose oxidation.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: In a pancreatic beta-cell, membrane depolarization has just opened voltage-gated calcium channels, and cytosolic calcium concentration is rising. Which of the following is the most direct consequence of this rise in cytosolic calcium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhibition of the K_ATP potassium leak channel

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased glucose entry through GLUT2

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vesicle fusion and exocytosis of stored insulin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxidative phosphorylation of imported glucose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Proteolytic cleavage of proinsulin to insulin

explanation.summary: Calcium influx is the final trigger that makes insulin-containing vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: Upon depolarization, voltage-gated calcium channels open and calcium flows down its concentration gradient into the cytosol. The increased cytosolic calcium activates proteins on membrane vesicles that contain pre-translated insulin, causing them to traffic to and fuse with the plasma membrane. This exocytosis is the last step (step 5) of the secretion sequence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: K_ATP inhibition is caused by ATP and occurs before depolarization, not after calcium entry.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GLUT2 transport is the first event of the sequence, driven by elevated blood glucose, not by calcium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxidation of glucose to generate ATP precedes channel closure and depolarization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Proinsulin processing is a post-translational modification that happens before storage in granules, not a response to calcium.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes mellitus has an undetectable C-peptide level. Tired of daily injections, she asks whether she could take a sulfonylurea tablet instead. Which of the following best explains why a sulfonylurea would not control her blood glucose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Her tissue insulin resistance blocks the drug's effect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her beta-cells cannot produce insulin for the drug to release

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug requires GLUT2, which type 1 beta-cells lack

choices.label: D
choices.text: Circulating C-peptide inactivates the drug in the bloodstream

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug opens rather than closes K_ATP in type 1 disease

explanation.summary: Sulfonylureas only augment secretion of endogenous insulin, so the patient must still be able to produce insulin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonylureas block the K_ATP channel to force depolarization and exocytosis of insulin that the beta-cell has already made. For this strategy to be viable, patients must be able to produce endogenous insulin. Her undetectable C-peptide indicates no beta-cell insulin production, so there is nothing for the drug to release.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Insulin resistance is the problem sulfonylureas are used to overcome in type 2 diabetes; her issue is absent production, not resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfonylureas act on the K_ATP channel, not through GLUT2, and GLUT2 is not the missing element in type 1 disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: C-peptide has no drug-inactivating role, and her C-peptide is undetectable anyway.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfonylureas close the K_ATP channel regardless of diabetes type.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes had a sulfonylurea added after a first-line agent failed to lower his glucose adequately. His control improved initially, but after several years of unchanged sedentary habits and diet his glucose is again poorly controlled despite the maximal sulfonylurea dose. Which of the following best explains the loss of benefit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The K_ATP channel has developed tolerance to the drug

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug has depleted his circulating C-peptide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chronic use has converted his disease to type 1

choices.label: D
choices.text: The underlying insulin resistance was never corrected

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug has suppressed incretin release after meals

explanation.summary: Boosting endogenous insulin is a stopgap; if insulin insensitivity persists, even augmented insulin eventually stops helping.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonylureas are used as add-on therapy when a first-line agent is not successful enough, but increasing endogenous insulin production is only a stopgap measure to overcome insulin insensitivity. If the underlying issue generating the dampened signaling remains unresolved, even the augmented amount of insulin produced will eventually no longer aid the patient. His unchanged lifestyle left the resistance in place.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tolerance at the channel is not the mechanism the brick describes; the failure is downstream at the level of tissue responsiveness.
whyWrongByChoice.B: C-peptide is co-secreted with insulin and is not depleted by the drug.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfonylureas do not transform type 2 diabetes into type 1 disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfonylureas act on the beta-cell K_ATP channel and do not suppress incretin hormones.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and obesity is prescribed a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, which her physician notes may also help with weight loss. GLP-1 belongs to which of the following hormone classes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An incretin that potentiates insulin action upon food intake

choices.label: B
choices.text: A sulfonylurea that blocks the beta-cell K_ATP channel

choices.label: C
choices.text: A counterregulatory hormone that liberates hepatic glycogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: An insulin analog engineered to resist oligomerization

choices.label: E
choices.text: An AMPK activator that drives GLUT4 to the muscle surface

explanation.summary: GLP-1 is an incretin, a hormone class that potentiates the action of insulin when food is consumed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metabolic regulation is not just the balance of insulin and glucagon. Incretins are a hormone class that potentiate the action of insulin upon food consumption. GLP-1 in particular has received considerable attention because agonists of its receptor are prescribed for diabetes and are being explored for weight loss.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Sulfonylureas are a drug class, not a hormone, and act by blocking the K_ATP channel.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucagon, not GLP-1, is the hormone that mobilizes hepatic glycogen to raise blood glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GLP-1 is a distinct peptide hormone, not a modified form of insulin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: AMPK is activated by rising AMP during energy expenditure, not by GLP-1.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A researcher tracks newly synthesized preproinsulin in a pancreatic beta-cell. The first processing step converts preproinsulin into proinsulin. Which of the following describes this step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cleavage of the C-peptide within secretory granules

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assembly into hexamers within the Golgi apparatus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Phosphorylation of the B chain at the plasma membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduction of A-B disulfide bonds within the cytosol

choices.label: E
choices.text: Removal of the N-terminal signal peptide in the ER

explanation.summary: Preproinsulin becomes proinsulin when the N-terminal signal peptide is removed in the endoplasmic reticulum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Before release, insulin undergoes extensive post-translational modification via proteolytic cleavage. First, during intracellular trafficking, the N-terminal signal peptide is removed within the endoplasmic reticulum, yielding proinsulin. Only later is the single chain converted into the disulfide-linked A-B heterodimer by cleavage and release of the C-peptide.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C-peptide release is the second cleavage, converting proinsulin to mature insulin, not preproinsulin to proinsulin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hexamer formation reflects self-oligomerization at high concentration in granules, not a processing step.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin maturation is accomplished by proteolysis, not phosphorylation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The disulfide bonds linking the A and B chains are retained in mature insulin, not reduced.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: Insulin stored in beta-cell granules is released into the bloodstream, where the concentrated hormone begins to dissociate. Which of the following statements about the different oligomeric forms of insulin is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hexamer binds the receptor with the highest affinity

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dimer is less active than the monomeric form

choices.label: C
choices.text: The monomer is the inactive storage form in granules

choices.label: D
choices.text: Self-oligomerization is favored at low concentration

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dilution in the bloodstream promotes hexamer assembly

explanation.summary: Activity ranks monomer > dimer > hexamer; the dimer is an intermediate that is less active than the monomer.
explanation.whyCorrect: At the high insulin concentration within granules, self-oligomerization is favored and insulin is predominantly a hexamer, which is inactive and cannot bind the receptor. Upon release into the high-volume bloodstream, dilution promotes dissociation of the oligomers. During dissociation of the hexamer, insulin can also be maintained as a dimer, which is less active than its monomeric form.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The hexamer is inactive and incapable of binding the insulin receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The monomer is the fully active form; the hexamer is the storage aggregate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oligomerization is favored at the high concentration found in granules, not at low concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dilution drives dissociation of oligomers, the opposite of assembly.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with type 1 diabetes uses a once-daily basal insulin that provides slow, prolonged release after subcutaneous injection. Which molecular property was most likely engineered into this long-acting formulation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Retention of the C-peptide to delay activation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Resistance to self-association so monomers form quickly

choices.label: C
choices.text: Addition of a signal peptide that slows tissue uptake

choices.label: D
choices.text: A primary sequence that favors oligomer formation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Removal of the disulfide bonds between A and B chains

explanation.summary: Long-acting insulins are engineered so that oligomers are favored, slowing the appearance of active monomer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Human insulin has been intentionally mutated to alter its oligomerization properties. Fast-acting insulin has its primary sequence altered to prevent oligomer formation, whereas oligomers are favored in slow or long-acting insulin. Because oligomers are inactive and must dissociate into monomers, favoring them produces a slow, sustained release of active hormone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: All purified injectable insulins lack the C-peptide; it is not used to modulate duration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Resistance to self-association is the fast-acting design, giving rapid onset rather than prolonged action.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The signal peptide is removed in the ER during normal processing and is not part of any injectable insulin design.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The A-B disulfide bonds define the functional mature hormone; removing them would not create a slow-release product.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: In the years following the 1921 identification of insulin in Toronto, patients with diabetes were treated with insulin isolated from pigs and dogs, with striking but limited success. Which of the following most limited the long-term success of these animal-derived preparations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Animal insulin was secreted without the C-peptide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Animal insulin was unable to form storage hexamers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eventual immune rejection of the foreign protein

choices.label: D
choices.text: Animal insulin could not activate the human receptor

choices.label: E
choices.text: The preparations lacked a functional A chain

explanation.summary: Pig and dog insulin worked but eventually failed because of immune rejection, driving the push for recombinant human insulin.
explanation.whyCorrect: For years after its discovery, pig and dog insulin were isolated to treat diabetics with resounding but limited success due to eventual immune rejection. Even though the primary sequence of human insulin was known, the disulfide pattern that gave rise to functional protein was elusive, and it took years of research before insulin became the first recombinant human protein to be commercially marketed in 1979.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lack of C-peptide is true of all purified injectable insulins and does not limit efficacy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oligomerization is not described as the limiting problem of animal insulin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Animal insulin clearly worked initially, so receptor activation was not the barrier.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The preparations were functional hormone; an absent A chain would have made them inactive from the start.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: Insulin binds its receptor on a skeletal muscle cell. Insulin receptor substrate localization, PI3-kinase activation, and PIP3 formation follow in sequence. Which of the following kinases then mediates the activation of Akt/PKB?

choices.label: A
choices.text: PDK-1

choices.label: B
choices.text: AMPK

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adenylate kinase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glycogen phosphorylase

choices.label: E
choices.text: PFK-1

explanation.summary: In the insulin receptor cascade, PDK-1 activates Akt/PKB downstream of PIP3 formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Insulin binding triggers signaling through insulin receptor substrate localization, PI3-kinase function, PIP3 formation, and PDK-1-mediated Akt/PKB activation. Activated PKB/Akt then drives the trafficking of GLUT4-rich vesicles to the plasma membrane.

whyWrongByChoice.B: AMPK is the energy sensor that promotes GLUT4 deposition independent of insulin, not the kinase that activates Akt.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adenylate kinase interconverts ADP into AMP and ATP; it is not part of the insulin receptor cascade.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycogen phosphorylase is a metabolic enzyme regulated by AMP, not a signaling kinase upstream of Akt.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PFK-1 is a glycolytic enzyme that senses AMP; it does not phosphorylate Akt.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: In an adipocyte, activated Akt/PKB promotes translocation of GLUT4-rich vesicles to the plasma membrane. Akt does so by activating a small G-protein of the Ras family, which in turn engages molecular motor proteins and SNARE complexes required for membrane fusion. Which of the following is that small G-protein?

choices.label: A
choices.text: PI3-kinase

choices.label: B
choices.text: PDK-1

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insulin receptor substrate

choices.label: D
choices.text: AMPK

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rab

explanation.summary: Rab, a Ras-family small G-protein activated by PKB/Akt, links insulin signaling to GLUT4 vesicle motors and SNARE-mediated fusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The broad molecular details of GLUT4 vesicle trafficking entail PKB/Akt activation of the small G-protein Rab, a Ras family member, with subsequent activation of molecular motor proteins and SNARE protein complexes required for membrane fusion. The precise details remain incompletely defined and are an area of intense research because of therapeutic ramifications.

whyWrongByChoice.A: PI3-kinase is a lipid kinase upstream of Akt that generates PIP3; it is not a small G-protein.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PDK-1 is the kinase that activates Akt, upstream of the vesicle trafficking step.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin receptor substrate is the adaptor localized to the activated receptor at the very top of the cascade.
whyWrongByChoice.D: AMPK is the AMP-activated kinase of the insulin-independent pathway, not a Ras-family G-protein.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A researcher engineers a muscle cell line in which no GLUT4 is stored in intracellular vesicles; instead, GLUT4 must be newly transcribed and translated whenever insulin binds. Compared with normal muscle, how would these cells respond to a glucose load in the presence of insulin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Faster uptake because the transporters are freshly synthesized

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delayed uptake that prolongs the hyperglycemic state

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unchanged uptake because GLUT2 substitutes for GLUT4

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediate uptake because insulin bypasses transcription

choices.label: E
choices.text: No uptake because GLUT4 only functions from vesicles

explanation.summary: Pre-translated GLUT4 pools allow a rapid response; relying on new transcription and translation would delay uptake and prolong hyperglycemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytosolic membrane-bound vesicles in adipocytes and skeletal muscle contain large amounts of pre-translated GLUT4. Using these pools allows a rapid response to stimuli to augment glucose uptake quickly. Because transcription and translation take additional time, a cell that had to make GLUT4 from scratch would respond late, prolonging the hyperglycemic state.

whyWrongByChoice.A: New synthesis adds time; it does not accelerate the response relative to deploying pre-made transporters.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Muscle uses GLUT4 for insulin-responsive uptake; GLUT2 is the beta-cell transporter and does not substitute.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Insulin's rapid effect depends on trafficking existing transporters; in this engineered cell that shortcut is removed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Once newly made GLUT4 reaches the surface it would function; the defect is delay, not complete absence of uptake.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: During prolonged nutrient restriction, AMPK becomes activated within pancreatic beta-cells. Which of the following best describes the effect of this activation on insulin secretion and the reason for it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased secretion, to promote glucose storage as glycogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased secretion, because AMPK closes the K_ATP channel

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unchanged secretion, because AMPK acts only in muscle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreased secretion, to favor catabolism over anabolism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Decreased secretion, because AMPK degrades insulin granules

explanation.summary: AMPK activation suppresses insulin secretion in beta-cells under low-energy conditions so that catabolism is favored.
explanation.whyCorrect: AMPK acts globally across tissues as a sensor of energy and nutritional status, promoting catabolism and inhibiting anabolism when ATP is depleted. AMPK activation has been shown to suppress insulin secretion in beta-cells under low-energy conditions to promote catabolism, since insulin is the anabolic hormone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Promoting glycogen storage is anabolic, the opposite of what AMPK signals in a low-energy state.
whyWrongByChoice.B: K_ATP closure is caused by rising ATP, which signals energy abundance; AMPK signals the opposite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: AMPK activity can be locally induced in many tissues, including beta-cells, not only muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brick describes suppression of secretion, not destruction of stored granules.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A region of skeletal muscle becomes ischemic. Even though the muscle is not contracting, AMPK activity in the affected cells increases markedly. Which of the following best explains this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ischemia raises ATP, which allosterically activates AMPK

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lack of oxygen blocks adenylate kinase, so ADP accumulates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anaerobic glycolysis makes less ATP than OXPHOS, raising AMP:ATP

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hypoxia stimulates insulin secretion, which activates AMPK

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ischemic muscle takes up AMP from the bloodstream

explanation.summary: Lack of oxygen is one of the conditions that raises the AMP:ATP ratio and activates AMPK, because anaerobic glycolysis yields far less ATP than OXPHOS.
explanation.whyCorrect: High AMP:ATP ratios that favor AMPK activity occur via nutrient restriction, lack of oxygen, or exercise-induced stress. Oxygen availability matters because anaerobic glycolysis produces less ATP than OXPHOS, so when oxygen is limited the cell cannot regenerate ATP efficiently, AMP rises via adenylate kinase, and AMPK is activated even without contraction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AMPK is activated by AMP, not ATP; rising ATP would indicate energy sufficiency and suppress the signal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Adenylate kinase is the enzyme that generates the AMP signal; it is not blocked by hypoxia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypoxia does not stimulate insulin secretion, and AMPK is not activated by insulin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The AMP signal is generated intracellularly by adenylate kinase, not imported from blood.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A sedentary 52-year-old man with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes is told to prioritize walking, cycling, swimming, and air squats. He asks why these are emphasized over strengthening his arms with small free weights. Which of the following best explains the recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their large muscle mass gives far greater glucose-clearing capacity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arm muscles lack any pre-translated GLUT4 vesicle pool

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leg muscles express the low-affinity GLUT2 transporter

choices.label: D
choices.text: AMPK can only be activated in lower-extremity muscles

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upper-body exercise suppresses beta-cell insulin secretion

explanation.summary: Glutes and quads are targeted because their large mass and surface area offer the greatest capacity for insulin-independent glucose transport.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bodily movement exhausts ATP to stimulate AMPK, which promotes deposition of high-affinity GLUT4 on the cell surface and aids insulin-independent glucose uptake. The glutes and quads are targeted specifically because of their large mass and surface area compared with other muscle groups; they offer a greater capacity to transport glucose and aid glucose clearance in the management of diabetes.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Skeletal muscle generally contains pre-translated GLUT4 vesicles; the difference is quantity of muscle, not presence of the pool.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GLUT2 is the pancreatic beta-cell transporter; skeletal muscle uses high-affinity GLUT4.
whyWrongByChoice.D: AMPK is activated by ATP expenditure in any contracting muscle, not exclusively the legs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Arm exercise is not harmful; providers simply encourage including the larger muscle groups.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: Measurements in skeletal muscle show adenine nucleotide concentrations at rest of roughly ATP 5 mM, ADP 1 mM, and AMP 0.15 mM. During exercise the values become roughly ATP 4 mM, ADP 1.5 mM, and AMP 0.6 mM. Based on these data, why does AMP rather than ATP or ADP serve as the cell's low-energy signal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AMP is the most abundant adenine nucleotide in muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: ATP concentration does not change at all during exercise

choices.label: C
choices.text: ADP is converted entirely to AMP by adenylate kinase

choices.label: D
choices.text: AMP is the direct product of ATP hydrolysis by myosin

choices.label: E
choices.text: AMP shows the largest fold change from a very low baseline

explanation.summary: Although AMP is vastly less abundant than ATP or ADP, its fold change during energy expenditure is far greater, making it a sensitive signal.
explanation.whyCorrect: While the overall concentrations of ATP and ADP are greater than AMP, the fold change in AMP concentration is exponentially higher. In the data given, ATP falls by about 20% and ADP rises by about 50%, whereas AMP rises roughly fourfold. AMP concentrations are vastly lower than ATP and ADP, but the magnitude of change is much greater, allowing AMP accumulation to be a critical biological signal of ATP expenditure sensed by PFK-1, glycogen phosphorylase, and AMPK.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AMP is the least abundant of the three; ATP is most abundant.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ATP does decrease during exercise, but only modestly relative to the change in AMP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adenylate kinase converts two ADP into one AMP plus one ATP; ADP is not fully converted, and its level actually rises here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ATP hydrolysis primarily yields ADP; AMP arises secondarily through adenylate kinase.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man with type 1 diabetes injects his usual insulin dose but is then called into an urgent meeting and skips lunch. Two hours later coworkers find him disoriented and confused, and he then has a generalized seizure. Which of the following best explains his neurological symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Insulin directly depolarizes cortical neurons

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inadequate glucose supply compromises CNS function

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess insulin produces an anion-gap acidosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin drives potassium out of neurons into blood

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insulin-triggered GLUT4 floods neurons with glucose

explanation.summary: Insulin shock harms the brain because hypoglycemia deprives the CNS of glucose, producing a spectrum from disorientation to seizures.
explanation.whyCorrect: Insulin shock results when excessive insulin produces harmfully low blood glucose. Injecting insulin without ingesting sufficient glucose is one of the two classic scenarios. The largest complication of severe hypoglycemia is compromised CNS function due to inadequate glucose supply, resulting in symptoms that span from disorientation to altered mental status to seizures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Insulin does not act as a neuronal depolarizing agent; the injury is metabolic substrate deprivation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin shock does not cause metabolic acidosis; a high anion gap is a feature of insulin absence, not excess.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Insulin traps potassium inside cells rather than expelling it, and this is not the cause of the CNS symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin drives glucose into muscle and fat via GLUT4, which lowers blood glucose and starves, rather than floods, the brain.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes becomes shaky and mildly confused at her office after taking insulin and skipping a meal. She is awake, conversant, and able to swallow; no intravenous access or medical equipment is available. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give a second dose of rapid-acting insulin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wait for the insulin to wear off on its own

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give a high-protein, low-carbohydrate snack

choices.label: D
choices.text: Give juice or candy with a high glycemic index

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold all food until she reaches a hospital

explanation.summary: For an insulin-shock patient who can eat, glucose-enriched food or juice is the practical remedy when IV dextrose is unavailable.
explanation.whyCorrect: The remedy for insulin shock is to raise blood glucose so the brain is no longer deprived. While IV dextrose is the quickest route, these individuals are rarely in a hospital where it can be readily provided. If the patient is capable of eating, glucose-enriched foods such as candy can aid them, and juice is essentially liquid sugar with a high glycemic index that can be swallowed easily.

whyWrongByChoice.A: More insulin would drive glucose even lower and worsen the shock.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Untreated hypoglycemia can progress to seizures, coma, or death; waiting is dangerous.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A low-carbohydrate snack does not deliver the rapid glucose needed to reverse the deficit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The strategy is to raise blood glucose immediately by whatever route the setting allows, not to delay.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man with type 1 diabetes is found by his spouse unresponsive with his jaw tightly clenched. She injects glucagon from the emergency kit he carries, and within minutes he becomes responsive. Which of the following best explains how the injection reversed his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It overrode insulin's suppression and liberated hepatic glycogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocked the insulin receptor tyrosine kinase in muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: It degraded the circulating insulin into inactive fragments

choices.label: D
choices.text: It forced GLUT4 internalization from the muscle surface

choices.label: E
choices.text: It closed beta-cell K_ATP channels to stop insulin release

explanation.summary: Injected glucagon bypasses insulin's suppression of glucagon secretion, and the bolus mobilizes hepatic glycogen to raise blood glucose.
explanation.whyCorrect: In emergency situations, glucagon injection can rescue patients from insulin shock, and select patients carry such shots for this reason. Insulin normally inhibits glucagon secretion, but the injection bypasses this suppression so that the bolus of glucagon overrides the action of insulin and promotes liberation of hepatic glycogen stores, restoring blood glucose.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucagon acts through its own signaling in the liver; it does not antagonize the insulin receptor kinase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucagon does not destroy insulin; it counteracts its metabolic effect by raising glucose output.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The rescue works by increasing glucose supply from the liver, not by removing transporters from muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Closing K_ATP channels would increase insulin secretion, the opposite of what is needed.

questions.topicName: Cell Signaling in Context: Fed and Fasting Metabolic State (2 of 2)
